problems.problem: Potential customer drop-off on web estimates if visitors do not have an active default email client installed or configured.
problems.label: inference
problems.basis: The contact form on https://walkerelectricidaho.com/contact/ indicates 'This opens your email app with the details filled in so you can review before sending', which fails if the browser or operating system lacks a default mail client.

problems.problem: Missed phone calls or delayed email responses during active on-site electrical work.
problems.label: hypothesis
problems.basis: For a solo electrician working in the field during business hours (7:00 AM - 5:00 PM), answering calls and manually replying to emails simultaneously may cause delays.

existingSolutions.solution: Standard server-side web form handler (e.g., standard website contact form plugin or email relay)
existingSolutions.addresses: Delivers estimate requests reliably into the owner's inbox without requiring the website visitor to open a third-party email application.

existingSolutions.solution: Solo-contractor field service mobile app (e.g., entry-level Jobber or Housecall Pro)
existingSolutions.addresses: Manages basic job scheduling, customer text dispatching, and quotes for an independent contractor.

feasibility.explanation: No ForgeX custom automation or catalog solutions are recommended because the company falls outside ForgeX's target business segment.

aiDelivery.explanation: AI agent deployment is not recommended for a single-operator electrical contractor that does not have high lead volume or administrative staff overhead.

humanReview: Owner manual review of any inbound project requests and estimates.

risks.description: Implementing automated dispatch or pipeline tools for a single-person trade business introduces unnecessary cost and operational overhead without sufficient job volume to justify it.
Client-side email forms expose contact email parameters in the user's browser, though risks remain minimal for basic contact details.

assumptions: No service pricing, diagnostic fees, or hourly rates are published on the website.

questions: How do you currently capture and track customer inquiries when you are on a job site?
Do website visitors experience friction using the estimate button that opens their local email application?

sourcesUsed.usedFor: Company identity, location, core trade services, operating hours, and single-electrician positioning.
Contact channels, service areas, and estimate request form functionality.
Service call diagnostics and troubleshooting workflow details.
Generator service offerings and pricing approach.
Local licensing, permits, and inspection coordination details.
Informational content review and software footprint verification.
Verification of pricing disclosures and customer education.

limitations: The website does not disclose specific staff counts, but explicitly markets 'One trusted electrician. Every project, big or small.', demonstrating it is an individual owner-operator rather than a 10-75 employee firm.
No state electrical license number is displayed on the website.
No published prices or fee ranges exist on the site.

qualification.rationale: Walker Electric LLC is outside ForgeX's target customer segment. ForgeX specifically targets owner-led home-service contractors with about 10 to 75 staff who pay for leads. Walker Electric describes itself on its homepage as 'One trusted electrician. Every project, big or small.', operating as a solo proprietor / single-electrician business. The company does not operate the team size, administrative overhead, or multi-channel lead flow required to justify ForgeX's automation services.
